entities.summary: Seuserenre Khyan was a Hyksos king of the Fifteenth Dynasty of Egypt, ruling over Lower Egypt in the second half of the 17th century BC. His reign marked the beginning of the end for the New Kingdom's power and paved the way for the rise of the Sea Peoples. Khyan's military campaigns expanded Egyptian control into Canaan, but his successors were eventually defeated by the Israelites. The Hyksos period's cultural achievements, including the development of a unique blend of Egyptian and Asiatic influences, would later be emulated by other civilizations. Khyan's legacy is also tied to the biblical account of the Israelites' conquest of Canaan, with many scholars believing that his reign was a key factor in the eventual decline of Egyptian power.
